# GitHub Actions workflows

The repository has 7 current workflow YAML files (plus this README). Ordinary verification keeps its existing workflow and check identities while sharing build/audit implementation. Release, publish and deployment jobs retain separate permissions and configured environment protections.

## Naming

File names are `<kind>-<subject>.yml` and each workflow's `name:` is `<Kind> / <subject>`, so the Actions sidebar, the file and the docs agree. Kinds: `ci` (verification on PRs and main), `scan` (scheduled and push security scans), `deploy`, `release` and `publish`. Job names, which are the check names on a PR, were deliberately left unchanged when the files were renamed on 2026-11-22, because a repository rule may require them by name.

| File | Name in Actions |
| --- | --- |
| `ci-dotnet.yml` | CI / .NET and repo checks |
| `ci-mailbox-worker.yml` | CI / mailbox-worker |
| `ci-auth-worker.yml` | CI / auth-worker |
| `scan-dependencies.yml` | Scan / dependency vulnerabilities |
| `deploy-demo.yml` | Deploy / demo Workers |
| `release-workers.yml` | Release / Workers |
| `release-dotnet.yml` | Release / .NET tool |
| `publish-nuget.yml` | Publish / NuGet |

## Current workflows

| Workflow | Triggers | Purpose and checks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [ci-dotnet.yml](ci-dotnet.yml) | Main push, PR to main, merge queue, manual | Build & Test, nonpublishing tool-package smoke, tested-owner coverage, Code Quality, Windows CLI boundaries, documentation links and paths ([check-docs](../../scripts/docs/check-docs.ts)), exact locked dependency graphs, verified snapshots and Dependency Review. |
| [scan-dependencies.yml](scan-dependencies.yml) | Monday 03:00 UTC, main push, PR to main, manual | Vulnerability Audit: locked restore with low-severity/direct/transitive audit, strict JSON evidence validation and deprecation report. |
| [ci-auth-worker.yml](ci-auth-worker.yml) | Main push and PR to main on authorization-Worker, mailbox-Worker source/scripts and OAuth example paths, manual | OAuth authorization Worker isolated verification without deployment credentials: provider-neutral issuer experiment, strict mailbox Worker typecheck and bundle, issuer and callback binding regressions, portable consent/sign-in tests and real workerd Durable Object tests, then anonymous read-only probes of the public demo's MCP and metadata. |
| [ci-mailbox-worker.yml](ci-mailbox-worker.yml) | Main push, PR to main, merge queue | Worker API, D1, MCP, C# compatibility and real Playwright browser checks with Chromium protection; retains browser evidence. |
| [release-dotnet.yml](release-dotnet.yml) | Manual on main, exact version | locked restore/build/test, validated .NET tool package and provenance, six platform archives, tag at the built commit and GitHub release. |
| [publish-nuget.yml](publish-nuget.yml) | Successful `Release / .NET tool` run on main, or manual exact version plus release run ID | Verify immutable source/run/artifact/tag identity, download that artifact, validate packages, then publish in the `nuget` environment. |
| [deploy-demo.yml](deploy-demo.yml) | Manual on main (repository or production scope), explicit push to `publish/demo` (repository scope), or exact verified owner comment on #236 (protected production only) | Require the selected SHA already on main and its Worker and OAuth verification runs on main to have passed (awaited while still running, never repeated), preserve existing `demo`/`db`, and enforce completed-only schema checks for all generic release paths (the exceptions are the default-off `apply_external_action_keys_schema`, `apply_owner_grants_schema`, `apply_app_webhooks_schema`, `apply_app_webhook_deliveries_schema`, `apply_owner_grant_approvals_schema` and `apply_owner_grant_decisions_schema` inputs of a manual production dispatch, which may apply only the owner-approved `external_action_keys`, `owner_grants`, `app_webhooks`, `app_webhook_deliveries`, `owner_grant_approvals` and `owner_grant_decisions` tables and indexes); confirm settings and published Agent Start, `/connect` and public MCP evidence. Production then updates the running `weave-auth-demo` code from its own settings, without touching its secrets, and a successful production deploy calls `release-workers.yml`. |
| [release-workers.yml](release-workers.yml) | Called by a successful production deploy, or manual on main with a full commit SHA | Require that commit's newest production deployment from main to have succeeded (proof it deployed, not that it is still served) and both Workers' `package.json` versions to agree, then tag `v<version>` at it and publish a GitHub Release from that version's [CHANGELOG](../../CHANGELOG.md) section ([script](../../typescript/mailbox-worker/scripts/tag-release.ts)). It never moves a tag that names another commit, so an unbumped version fails here; a tag and release already at that commit are left as they are. |

Path-scoped workflows retain their original path filters; Host acceptance also runs when its shared build/setup action changes. This does not turn every change into every optional acceptance run. See each workflow for its exact paths, timeouts and artifact retention. CI retains test/coverage evidence for 30 days; dependency audit evidence is retained for 14 days.

## Shared implementation

- [setup-dotnet](../actions/setup-dotnet/action.yml) installs the `10.x` SDK channel (`dotnet-quality`, default `ga`) for the .NET 10 targets and runtime, and the `11.x` channel (`dotnet-next-quality`, default `ga`) with optional NuGet caching. `global.json` uses an `11.0.100` baseline (the first SDK whose compiler, Roslyn 5.12, can load the source generator's `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp` 5.12.0 reference) with `latestMajor` and `allowPrerelease: false`, so builds select the newest installed .NET 11 GA SDK. The setup action intentionally omits `global-json-file`, which would additionally install that baseline as an exact SDK. Locked dependency verification and security audits remain required when the selected SDK changes. The NuGet publishing job installs the `11.x`/`ga` SDK through its pinned setup action directly because it checks out validation code only; its sparse checkout still includes the root `global.json`, so it needs an SDK that satisfies the baseline.
- [strict-nuget-audit](../actions/strict-nuget-audit/action.yml) is shared by Code Quality in `ci-dotnet.yml` and `scan-dependencies.yml`. It validates machine-readable audit results using [check_dependency_audit.py](../../scripts/check_dependency_audit.py); restore failure, malformed/missing evidence, reported warnings/errors or any reported vulnerability fail the job.

## Retired checks and compatibility

The old `vertical-slice-validation.yml` and `security-release-chain-validation.yml` branch-specific workflows are removed. Their useful package smoke and strict audit checks now run in normal CI/security scanning. Their automatic lockfile regeneration/commit jobs are retired; normal CI validates committed lockfiles without rewriting or pushing them.

The PR190 exact-base coverage collector is no longer invoked by CI. Its old check name, **Exact-base coverage (diagnostic only)**, remains temporarily so an unverified required-check setting cannot be left waiting for a missing name. It now depends on the actual **Build & Test** job and fails unless that job succeeds. It performs no baseline collection, rebuild, threshold exception or fabricated success. The standalone diagnostic script and its safety tests remain available for deliberate local use.

Required-check/ruleset configuration could not be verified because the read endpoint was denied. Job names and the dependency scan's push/PR triggers therefore remain (file names and workflow names were changed on 2026-11-22; see Naming). Shared composite steps reduce duplicated maintenance without moving checks into nested reusable workflows or broadening path triggers to run unrelated suites. Release/publish/deployment workflows are not combined across credential or approval boundaries.

On 2026-11-22 the owner removed ten workflows that no longer served the current focus: the optional C# acceptance runs (Codex Bridge contract, First Use, dependency-policy acceptance, Echo plugin examples), the npm Echo plugin build, publish and published-package verification, and three one-time operations (the approved legacy-human D1 migration, the read-only D1 inventory and Cloudflare audit check, and the first-party OAuth issuer deployment); the `build-standalone-host` action they shared went with them. Their scripts stay in the repository for deliberate local use, and git history keeps the workflows. These changes do not delete historical Actions UI entries or run evidence. In particular, historical **Prepare PR90 Merge** came from `pr90-merge-preparation.yml`, which is not a current workflow file; it is distinct from the retired security-release-chain validation file.

## Release and deployment setup

NuGet publishing uses the existing `NUGET_API_KEY` Secret in its applicable scope and the `nuget` environment. Automatic publication is tied to one successful `Release / .NET tool` run. Manual republication requires the exact version and that run's ID; it does not select the latest release. Missing/expired/mismatched artifacts fail validation. There is no rebuild-from-source fallback. Packages use embedded symbols; the current release generates `.nupkg` only. `--skip-duplicate` handles an already-published version without selecting another version.


Worker deployment uses existing `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` and `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` Secrets. Manual dispatch on `main` selects repository or production scope; production retains its environment protections. An additional exact `/weave-deploy-demo` comment by the verified GitHub member `ldsenow` on issue #236 is supported for connected clients without `workflow_dispatch`. The workflow requires the exact owner, issue, non-PR conversation, `MEMBER` relationship and comment body, and independently rechecks the selected `main` SHA before and after the **existing protected production** approval. This path cannot select a new OAuth bootstrap or any data migration; it always uses `completed-only` and the existing Cloudflare secret. Other comments must skip all jobs. The release only succeeds after post-deploy `/connect` and MCP validation. This trigger does not give ChatGPT direct Cloudflare token access. An explicit push of an already-merged commit to `publish/demo` instead selects repository scope and automatically performs verified completed-only deployment without schema migration. Treat that branch as a release signal, not an ordinary working branch. Normal main pushes do not deploy. The selected SHA must already be on main and pass the verification job. Do not force-update the release branch or treat local checks as deployment authorization. No D1 ID/name, registration or host GitHub settings are required: existing D1 identity is discovered through the Worker binding, registration follows checked-in configuration (enabled for this public demo, with a total-account cap of 100, 10 registrations per source IP per hour, and 100 globally per hour), and new addresses use request origin. This is a demo only: data may be periodically cleared; do not store sensitive or important information. See [Worker deployment instructions](../../typescript/mailbox-worker/README.md#deploy-the-existing-worker-and-d1-database). Configured environment protection rules still apply. Local CI/fixture success is not evidence of a successful remote deployment.


Browser installation and focused verification commands are documented in [browser testing](../../docs/browser-testing.md). CI and release tests use the browser selected by the pinned .NET Playwright SDK; Worker verification uses its pinned Node SDK. No workflow should return to direct Chrome startup or debugging-port polling.
